segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Good morning Sarah, come in and have a seat. Yes, sorry for the mess, it's a Monday.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Haha yes that's fine, it's fine.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Okay so we have a six month follow-up on your sertraline. Let me just open your chart here for a moment.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Okay it looks like last time was in March, is that correct?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes that's right.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Good. And how have things been generally since then, mood-wise?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Hmm, I'd say it's been quite stable. There was a difficult period in August when I was struggling, but it resolved on its own. I think it was mostly work stress.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Okay, work stress. What was happening at work?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: We had a big deadline and I was the project lead. It was very intense, but it's over now.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: And sleep?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sleep is okay, seven to eight hours mostly. I don't wake up at night anymore like I used to, that's better.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: That sounds good. And you're still taking sertraline fifty milligrams in the morning?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, always in the morning with food.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Perfect. Any side effects you want to mention? Nausea or...

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, not really. Maybe a bit of dry mouth now and then, but nothing that bothers me.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: That's completely normal with sertraline. It's nothing we need to do anything about.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Okay, fine.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Let me take your blood pressure quickly.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Okay, one hundred eighteen over seventy-four. That's excellent Sarah.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh good!

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Yes, very good. And your weight, we weighed you last in March. Do you remember what you weighed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Hmm, I think it was sixty-three point five kilos or thereabouts.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Yes, sixty-three point five kilos, and now you're... hmm, sixty-eight kilos actually.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh really? I've been running quite a bit actually.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Interesting. Now I need to ask you about allergies because we need to update the chart. You have a penicillin allergy, correct?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I've had that since I was a teenager. It was quite severe—I got anaphylaxis, my throat swelled up, the whole thing.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Okay, so that's a confirmed anaphylactic reaction. It's important we always have that in the chart.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Of course.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: And latex, you mentioned that last time.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, latex too. That's mostly contact eczema, nothing serious but it's uncomfortable.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Yes, we use nitrile gloves here so that's fine. Now, your mother has Type 2 diabetes, correct?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, she was diagnosed when she was fifty-eight. And my father... well, he had a heart attack. He survived thankfully, but he was only forty-five at the time.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: That's concerning given your family history. We should monitor your cholesterol and blood sugar. Let's do a blood test next time.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: That sounds reasonable.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: And your emergency contact—is it still your brother Thomas?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, Thomas Lindqvist. His number is forty 4099 2231.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Forty 4099 2231, okay I have that.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: And the cetirizine for seasonal allergies, are you still taking that?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, but I take it year-round now, not just spring and summer like before. Actually I'm taking it twice a day.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Hmm, okay. That's an as-needed medication, so ideally it should be seasonal. Why the change?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I just felt like my allergies were worse this year. But actually I've also started taking ibuprofen daily for inflammation, is that okay?

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Daily ibuprofen? How much and for how long?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Four hundred milligrams every morning, been doing it for about two months now. My knees have been bothering me from running.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Okay, that's new and not something in your chart. We should discuss this more. Is there anything else you want to talk about today?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Actually yes, I recently changed jobs. I'm now an engineer at Lama Bank in Copenhagen.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Oh, how exciting.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, it's much more interesting work, and I'm not commuting as much. Actually, I moved to Copenhagen three months ago.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Oh, so you won't be my patient for much longer.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I need to find a new doctor in Copenhagen, but I wanted to have this follow-up with you since I know you.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Of course, that's completely fine. I'll write a summary letter for your new doctor. Should we say six months again or would you like a shorter interval?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Six months is fine, I'm doing well.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: Perfect. So we continue with sertraline fifty milligrams, no dose change. And you or rather your new doctor will see you in six months.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thank you, Doctor Holm.

segments.speaker: DR_HOLM
segments.text: You're welcome, Sarah. Take care of yourself. Goodbye.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Goodbye.
